working_read,"Latest (Wed 8:18 AM ET): DOT's written release quotes Duffy saying investigators have recreated the El Dorado overload in the L3Harris lab but still lack a root cause (Confirmed). Three new Reported threads point at process, not just hardware: the Washington Post says an FAA official supervised and signed off on the El Dorado work minutes before the network faltered; KATV reports a 2025 FAA procedure change that auto-approves contractor upgrades; and a CRN source says the device's broadcast/multicast feature should have been off. All single-source. Still no written root cause, FBI or CISA finding, IG or NTSB review, or hearing date. Latest (Tue

Tue,DOT: investigators recreated the El Dorado overload in the lab; root cause still unclear,"DOT's written release of Duffy's Senate remarks: ""We've been able to recreate what happened in El Dorado, but the root cause of what happened, we don't have clarity yet."" He says this was the 69th installation of that router (68 worked), that L3Harris, HPE, Cisco, the FAA and an FBI team are at the L3Harris lab in Florida, and that national security agencies told him ""we weren't hacked."" Reuters separately reports Duffy saying no root cause has been determined. [DOT release](https://www.transportation.gov/briefing-room/icymi-trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-shares-update-nationwide-ground) · [Reuters via Investing.com](https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/root-cause-of-us-aviation-shutdown-not-yet-determined-duffy-says-4965705)",C
Tue,"Washington Post: an FAA official supervised, tested and signed off on the El Dorado work minutes before the network faltered","Citing a person familiar with the investigation, the Post reports an FAA official was on site supervising the contractor's copper-to-fiber switch, tested the finished work and signed off about eight minutes before the radio network began to falter; the source says the exact cause is not confirmed. Asked for comment, the FAA pointed to Duffy's Tuesday remarks. Single-source; not confirmed by the FAA. [Washington Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/transportation/2026/11/17/faa-oversaw-signed-off-repair-work-before-nationwide-ground-stop/) · [Mashable](https://sea.mashable.com/tech/56956/faa-official-oversaw-router-work-just-before-nationwide-ground-stop-report-claims)",Reported
Tue,KATV: internal FAA documents show reduced FAA review of contractor work at telecom sites,"KATV (Little Rock) says internal documents show a draft procedure, put into effect by a May 20, 2025 memo, that treats contractor upgrades such as copper-to-fiber conversions and router swaps as automatically approved ""maintenance notifications"" instead of FAA-reviewed requests; a DOT source is anonymous and the documents are not public. [KATV](https://katv.com/news/local/internal-documents-reveal-faa-reduced-maintenance-oversight-before-ground-stop-travelers-airlines-contractors-upgrades-sop-telecommunications-sites-national-airspace-system-infrastructure-el-dorado)",Reported
Tue,CRN source: the El Dorado device is a copper-to-fiber converter with a multicast feature,"A source close to the incident told CRN no one has determined the Juniper device malfunctioned, that it is a copper-to-fiber communications device with a multicast feature rather than strictly a router, and that its broadcast feature appears to have been on while talking to legacy Cisco routers (""should not have been turned on""). HPE told CRN Monday its equipment ""was working as configured."" [CRN](https://www.crn.com/news/networking/2026/faa-stops-installation-of-hpe-juniper-routers-in-wake-of-ground-stop-investigation)",Reported`,
